data.body:
AC3 IS NOW MET. Recording the attestation the criterion asks for — and correcting my own process error, which the completion verifier caught.

**The evidence.**

    workflow:  test.yml ("Test Suite")
    run id:    33967035958
    event:     schedule
    branch:    main
    headSha:   0033662b5534531d84e39d4a14bf75c8e768e85e
    job:       build-and-test / pytest (ubuntu-latest, py3.13)
    result:    completed / SUCCESS

    also on that run: build-and-test / pytest (macos-latest, py3.13) -> completed / success

The sha contains this ticket's fix: `git merge-base --is-ancestor c4e43e3f9a4d 0033662b5534` returns
true. `main`'s history from the fix forward is `c4e43e3f9a4d` (2669, this fix) -> `adfc5285fad6` ->
`cf9c3daf9922` -> `8629e3874aea` -> `59d504c2bdbb` -> `0033662b5534`.

This is the run the criterion was written for: a SCHEDULED `test.yml` run, on `main` itself, on a sha
carrying the fix, with the named gating cell passing. Not a patchset, not an inference. For contrast,
the same cell FAILED on `a33333b8709a` (run 33950878570) and on `9d5a7278c892` (run 33956014400),
both of which predate the fix.

`main` is excluded from `test.yml`'s push triggers, so this could only ever arrive on the
`41 */6 * * *` schedule. It fired at 12:47 UTC and the gating cell completed successfully.

**My process error, since it is the more useful part of this comment.** I ticked AC3 and immediately
ran the close. The completion verifier refused with:

> No attestation of a scheduled `test.yml` run on `main` at sha `c4e43e3f9a4d` or any later sha is
> visible in the ticket snapshot. The criterion was deliberately left unticked pending a natural
> scheduled run.

It was right. I had the run in front of me and ticked the box on the strength of that, but never
wrote the evidence into the ticket — so the only AC3 material in the snapshot was my earlier INTERIM
comment, which explicitly says the evidence it presents is insufficient. The verifier read the ticket
faithfully and reached the only conclusion the ticket supported.

Worth naming plainly: a ticked checkbox is an ASSERTION, and the verifier does not take assertions.
It reads the record. Ticking a box while the supporting evidence lives only in the closer's working
context produces exactly this refusal, and the refusal is the system working. Had it accepted the
tick, this ticket would have closed claiming a CI attestation that appeared nowhere in it — which is
the failure mode the whole gate exists to prevent.

The verifier's second finding follows from the first and is likewise satisfied by the run above: the
bug's core observable — the gating cell being RED on `main` — is now directly measured as green on a
sha containing the fix, so the reported defect no longer reproduces.

Re-running the close now that this is on the record.
